newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president's son appears for questioning.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president's son appears for questioning.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's son appeared at state prosecution offices for questioning on Thursday on suspicion of taking kickbacks and influence-peddling.
Television pictures showed Kim Hyun-chul arriving at the Supreme Public Prosecutors' Office in Seoul. Prosecution sources said the younger Kim would be arrested, probably this week.
South Korean prosecutors have traditionally announced the summoning of suspected criminals only when they have secured evidence to charge them.
During parliamentary hearings over a loans-for-kickbanks scandal surrounding Hanbo, Kim Hyun-chul denied he took bribes from companies or meddled in state affairs.
"Prosecutors have secured enough evidence to charge him for criminal offences," one prosecution official said. He gave no other details.

Prosecutors said they had traced more than 100 bank accounts of Kim Hyun-chul's close associates and their relatives to find out if the president's son accepted kickbacks in return for peddling influence.
